question: Which of the following is a MACROVASCULAR complication of diabetes mellitus?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nephropathy (glomerular disease) is a microvascular complication caused by damage to the small vessels of the glomerulus.
Retinopathy is a microvascular complication affecting the small retinal vessels.
Correct. Peripheral arterial disease, coronary artery disease, and stroke are macrovascular complications of diabetes.
Peripheral neuropathy is classified as a microvascular/neural complication, not macrovascular.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: microvascular = retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy (the 3 Ns + R). Macrovascular = large vessel disease (CAD, stroke, PAD).
Well done — peripheral arterial disease is a macrovascular complication. Macrovascular = large vessels (CAD, stroke, PAD).
